title: Closed constant coefficient tensors and pullback on the etale site
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $X$ a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with constant ring sheaves $A_T$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] and ordinary module sheaves on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]. For a closed immersion $i:C\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] set $P_C=i_*A_C$, with underived direct image [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], in degree zero. For every scheme morphism $v:X'\to X$, put $C'=X'\times_XC$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Pullback of locally constant sections on $C\times_XT$, for each etale $T\to X$, defines $P_C\to v_*P_{C'}$. Its adjoint, for the constant-ring inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], is an isomorphism
$$b_{v,C}:v^{-1}P_C\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{C'}.$$
It carries the restriction $A_X\to P_C$ to $A_{X'}\to P_{C'}$. These particular isomorphisms preserve identities and compositions under the canonical composition isomorphism for inverse images.

For closed immersions $C,D\hookrightarrow X$, put $I=C\times_XD$. Restrict locally constant sections on $C\times_XT$ and $D\times_XT$ to $I\times_XT$ and multiply. This gives an isomorphism of sheaf tensors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]
$$\mu_{C,D}:P_C\otimes_{A_X}P_D\xrightarrow{\sim}P_I.$$
Every $P_C$ is flat, meaning that tensoring with it is an exact functor [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Consequently the same map on degree-zero flat models gives $\mu_{C,D}:P_C\otimes_A^LP_D\xrightarrow{\sim}P_I$ in the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], with derived tensor as in [def-kun-derived-tensor] and total tensor as in [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. Under the canonical associators, $\mu_{I,E}(\mu_{C,D}\otimes1)=\mu_{C,D\cap E}(1\otimes\mu_{D,E})$ for every third closed $E$, and $\mu_{D,C}\sigma=\mu_{C,D}$ after the support-interchange identification. For $D'=X'\times_XD$, $I'=X'\times_XI$, the canonical tensor comparison gives
$$b_{v,I}\circ v^{-1}\mu_{C,D}=\mu_{C',D'}\circ(b_{v,C}\otimes b_{v,D}).$$
The same equalities hold for the displayed derived tensors. No finite-type, separatedness, reducedness, or Cartier hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tag 03Q1, lemma-stalk-pullback, especially (3); agent-formulated closed-constant tensor refinement of the stalk calculation, retained from returned item Step 2. Tensor multiplication and flatness are assertions of this lemma, not assertions attributed to Tag 03Q1 alone.

proof.text: Normalize the constant-module transition map on the tensor unit, and identify the section A_X → i_*A_C with the lax unit comparison of i_*. The open-closed short exact sequence makes this section an epimorphism. These are the specified maps, not replacement choices.

Restricting the section to C gives the adjunction-unit isomorphism. The inverse-image/stalk comparison therefore makes the section an isomorphism at each geometric point factoring through C. Outside C, factor through the open complement and use open-closed vanishing; the stalk is zero. Closed immersions remain closed under the fiber products and compositions used for intersections.

Identify the canonical pullback adjoint on the tensor unit with the finite base-change mate. Its mate is monoidal: prove this by expanding adjunction units and naturality. Since a closed immersion is finite, its base-change map is invertible. Cancel the epimorphic section to identify this invertible mate with the specified pullback adjoint; the same unit computation proves its restriction compatibility.

For identity and composition, cancel the corresponding epimorphic constant section after inverse image. The canonical inverse-image composition and identity unit equations, and monoidal unit naturality, identify both composites. The support-change maps are normalized by the constant transition-unit calculation.

The tensor of two epimorphic sections is epimorphic since each sheaf tensor functor is a left adjoint. Multiplication composed with this tensor is the unit multiplication followed by the intersection section. At a point on both supports all three section maps are invertible, so multiplication is invertible. Otherwise a source tensor factor and the target are zero. Geometric-stalk conservativity proves invertibility.

Use the existing stalkwise flatness criterion. On the support the epimorphic constant section is an isomorphism on stalks, by step 2; the stalk of its source is flat because a monoidal stalk functor sends the tensor unit to the free rank-one A-module. Off the support the stalk is zero by step 2, and zero is flat. Thus every geometric stalk is flat.

Cancel the epimorphic tensor of three sections to verify associativity, and two sections to verify symmetry. Naturality of the associator and braiding and their coherence on the tensor unit reduce both to the normalized support-transition maps.

Cancel the inverse image of the epimorphic tensor of sections. Oplax tensor naturality, the unit axiom, and the computed compatibility of the pullback adjoints and support changes with sections prove the ordinary pullback square.

Apply the generic canonical flat degree-zero pairing compatibility lemma to the ordinary associativity, symmetry and inverse-image squares of steps 7 and 8, using flatness from step 6 for the left factors. The derived multiplication is invertible because its canonical flat-model comparison and the ordinary multiplication are invertible. These are exactly the displayed derived maps by the explicit singleFunctorFlatPairing interface.

proof_origin.place: U4 stage-3 reduction: unit-section epimorphisms, finite base change, unit/zero stalks and categorical coherence; the separate source result about canonical flat degree-zero pairings supplies step 9. Flatness reuses the unit/zero stalk computations of the proof. Target statement and the unit route are unchanged.

Its tensor functors therefore encode exactly the site tensor and exact tensoring recorded by def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product and def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules, in the accepted fixed-coefficient encoding; no alternative tensor construction is introduced. U4 preserves all statement signatures. Their bodies contain no choices and are definitionally the previous composites. Five change records document the interfaces.
